I am a woman of 35 with no schooling, farming less than one hectare of maize here in Mangochi. My husband and I depend on this plot for our food, so I must try hard. If I get a coupon from the government this year, I will buy NPK and urea — without it, fertilizer is too expensive and I will use only a little. I keep some chickens and a goat, so I put their manure on the field, and I intercrop with pigeon pea and pumpkin to help the soil and feed my children.
